merger_name: Vopak Terminals Sydney – Leasehold interest in land at Port Botany, NSW

anzsic_codes.name: Port and Water Transport Terminal Operations

merger_description:
Vopak Terminals Sydney Pty Limited (**Vopak**) is a subsidiary of Dutch-based and listed Koninklijke Vopak N.V., a global infrastructure and logistics provider for storing and handling bulk liquids and gases. The main shareholder of the Vopak group is HAL Holding N.V., an international investment company listed on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange via HAL Trust.

Port Botany is a container port and common user bulk liquids facility in Sydney.

Port Botany Operations Pty Ltd, as trustee of the Port Botany Unit Trust (**PBOL**), is a member of the NSW Ports group (**NSW Ports**). NSW Ports owns and operates Port Botany and Port Kembla under long-term leases granted by the NSW Government. Through PBOL, NSW Ports provides port infrastructure and land management services and grants leases and subleases to port users.

Vopak operates a liquid fuel storage terminal at Port Botany, supplying liquid fuel storage and handling services to third parties. Vopak does not import and distribute fuel itself but supplies port-side infrastructure for third parties to import, store and distribute their fuel products.

Vopak proposes to build a new liquid fuel storage terminal at Port Botany and connect it with its existing terminal. The new terminal is intended for the storage and handling of jet fuel. However, it may alternatively be used for the storage and handling of diesel fuel, depending on future market demand and operational requirements.

Accordingly, Vopak has entered into an Agreement for Lease and Lease (involving a sublease) of certain land at 39 Friendship Road, Port Botany, NSW with PBOL, for the purposes of developing the new liquid fuel storage terminal. The land which is the subject of the proposed lease is currently unused.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is no horizontal consolidation or removal of a
competitor as a result of the Acquisition
b. the presence of alternative suppliers of liquid fuel storage
and handling services in New South Wales.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
